data.title: Microsoft draws mixed signals as hedge funds reshuffle positions in Q3
data.description:
Hedge fund positioning in Microsoft (MSFT) was mixed in Q3 2026, with several prominent investors initiating new positions while others reduced or exited existing holdings. The activity points to differing views on the software and cloud computing giant.

The most notable new positions included Third Point, led by Dan Loeb, which initiated a position of approximately 450,000 Microsoft shares. Soros Capital, led by Robert Soros, also opened a new position of 954 shares, while Thiel Macro, led by Peter Thiel, initiated a smaller stake of 2,000 shares. Discovery Capital, led by Rob Citrone, likewise established a new position of about 46,000 shares.

On the other hand, Pershing Square, led by Bill Ackman, reduced its Microsoft holdings by ~35%, from 6.21M shares to 4.06M shares. Altimeter Capital Management, led by Brad Gerstner, reduced its Microsoft exposure during Q3, cutting its holdings by approximately 7% to 1.18M shares from 1.27M shares. Soros Fund, led by George Soros, also trimmed its position, lowering its holdings from approximately 190,000 shares to 122,000 shares. 

Viking Global, led by Andreas Halvorsen, took a more decisive step, exiting its Microsoft position entirely after holding approximately 1.46M shares in the previous quarter. The full exit represents one of the more notable institutional departures from the stock during Q3. Corvex Management, led by Keith Meister, also exited its 132,000-share position entirely.

Some prominent investors maintained their exposure. Tiger Global, led by Chase Coleman, held ~2.27M Microsoft shares unchanged during the quarter.

data.title: Anthropic faces rocky next 60 to 90 days – analyst
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) faces a turbulent 60 to 90 days ahead following its initial public offering, according to Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets.

In an interview with CNBC, the longtime tech analyst warned that the AI company has "volatility and kind of lack of control of destiny" written all over its near-term outlook.

The assessment came as Anthropic (ANT) shares traded down approximately 10% on their first full day of trading after pricing the IPO at $83 per share and briefly hitting $110.

Kulkarni pointed to competitive pressure as a key concern, noting that OpenAI (OPENAI) launched a major model on Nov. 17 and Google (GOOGL), (GOOG) followed on Nov. 18 with Gemini 4—timing he suggested was not coincidental.

Beyond the competitive landscape, Kulkarni highlighted several structural headwinds facing the company. Lockup expirations begin as early as Dec. 15, with new shares coming to market roughly every three weeks thereafter. The analyst also noted that Anthropic's (ANT) SpaceX (SPCX) deal contributed to “mild margins” in Q3, a dynamic expected to continue through Q4 and Q1.

"There are a lot of external factors here that investors are going to take a step back and say, 'Hey, by the way, does this company control its own destiny?’" Kulkarni said.

He characterized the situation as "not a failed IPO, but it's just going to be a very, very, very rocky ride for Anthropic for the next 60, 90 days."

Looking ahead, Kulkarni acknowledged potential bright spots, particularly around revenue trends. He noted that annual run rate revenue figures for November and December will be crucial not only for Anthropic (ANT) but for "the entire AI narrative," as the industry enters a critical phase of understanding how pricing affects demand.

With Anthropic's (ANT) first earnings report not expected until February, Kulkarni suggested that incremental net adds exceeding $6B or $7B could represent a positive catalyst.

Until then, investors face a period of limited visibility as the company navigates competitive pressures and ongoing questions about its path forward.

data.title: Apple in spotlight as UBS weighs in on iPhone Duo wait times
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) was in the spotlight on Friday as investment firm UBS weighed in on the decline in wait times for the iPhone Duo.

Shares were modestly higher in late morning trading.

Wait times for the foldable smartphone have declined around 21 days on average to roughly 53 days, according to the investment firm's Evidence Lab, which tracks such data, analyst David Vogt said. 

Vogt also noted that there is no wait time for the iPhone 18 Pro, roughly in-line with what happened last year, while the wait time for the iPhone 18 Pro Max is down 1 day to roughly 5 days.

“The shortening in wait times means that availability for the Duo improves from late January to early January on average,” Vogt wrote in a note to clients. “Last earnings call, Apple noted that it is working to improve supply of the device but did not specify a timeline. On the other hand, the delta could suggest that consumers are either cancelling their order or deferring their purchase for a potential second-generation foldable. As such, we believe that it is too early to determine the driver for the WoW change.”

Vogt has a Neutral rating and a $340 price target on Apple.

Intuit stock slides as Credit Karma revenue growth outlook resets lower
data.description:
Intuit (INTU) stock dropped 9.7% in late morning trading on Friday as a higher-for-longer rate environment and AI's impact dimmed the outlook for the company's Credit Karma revenue growth.

"Strong Global Business Solutions and EPS execution were overshadowed by a Credit Karma-led FY27 revenue cut and weak Q2 guide," Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Wood wrote in a note to clients. He rates the stock at Equalweight and reduced his price target to $335 from $400.

The company, which also owns TurboTax and QuickBooks, pared its FY2027 revenue guidance to $23.08B-$23.37B, indicating it will miss the Visible Alpha consensus of $23.4B, from its prior range of $23.28B-$23.51B. Intuit Chief Financial Officer Sandeep Aujla told Seeking Alpha that the Federal Reserve's rate increase lowered demand for Credit Karma. Meanwhile, AI impacted the unit's business by more than it anticipated and faster than it had previously expected.

"The reduction reflects a reset in expected Credit Karma growth to 3–7% from 11–13%, equating to a ~$173M revenue reduction at the midpoint, which accounts for the majority of the FY27 guidance change," Evercore ISI analyst Kirk Materne wrote in a note to clients. He keeps his Outperform rating on the stock.

Oppenheimer analyst Scott Schneeberger, who has an Outperform rating on Intuit (INTU) noted that the company sees the slowing Credit Karma revenue growth as fixable, rather than structural, by applying the playbook it has used for TurboTax/QuickBooks.

Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin, with an Equalweight rating on the stock, said the fix for Credit Karma (LLM content, brand campaign, and engagement) will likely be gradual. He lowered his price target to $320 from $330.

The company also said on Thursday it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (BSP) for $3.68B, the proceeds of which will be used to buy back shares. The pending transaction "is a strategic positive — it  removes a business (that) guided flat-to-down and adds ~60 bps to company revenue growth," Morgan Stanley's Wood said.

Schneeberger also sees the divestiture as a positive. "Although Intuit acquired Mailchimp for ~$12B in 2021, we view this sale price favorably, as the transaction removes a distraction/overhang," he wrote.

"The prospect of shedding some baggage through the Mailchimp sale is positive, but INTU still faces an uphill climb with investors, and the Credit Karma shortfall doesn’t help," Evercore ISI's Materne wrote. "At 13.9x CY28 GAAP EPS, we believe the shares are largely washed out, but patience will be needed as we see few catalysts on the horizon."

The SA Quant system rates Intuit (INTU) a Hold, while the average SA Analyst rating  and the average  Wall Street rating sit at Buy.

data.title: Bending Spoons projects Q4 revenue of $984M-$1B while outlining $3.68B Mailchimp deal
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Bending Spoons S.p.A. (BSP) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Luca Ferrari said, "In Q3, revenue increased 125% to $780 million" and added that "Organic revenue growth was 3%," while noting that "Growth trends across most of our businesses were broadly consistent with Q2."
  • CEO Ferrari highlighted closed M&A, saying, "During the quarter, we announced the acquisitions of Airtable and Miro for a combined enterprise value of $2.65 billion. These acquisitions have now closed," and added on Airtable execution, "Since acquisition, we have already shipped 60 product improvements."
  • CEO Ferrari announced a new pending deal: "Yesterday, we announced the agreement to acquire Mailchimp from Intuit for an enterprise value of $3.68 billion," and said, "Mailchimp generated $1.27 billion in revenue in the 12 months to October 31," adding, "We see opportunities to improve the technology, product and monetization through our platform."
  • CEO Ferrari pointed to near-term acceleration claims in three turned-around assets: "Based on the work done in Q3 and prior quarters, all 3 are positioned to accelerate growth in Q4" (AOL, Eventbrite, Vimeo), and said at AOL, "The disruption to advertising performance was broadly in line with expectations and the gap in impression pricing relative to Yahoo!'s stack had largely closed by mid-September."
  • CEO Ferrari flagged uneven performance across the portfolio: "Revenues at Brightcove and Remini, for example, continue to decline," while also stating, "Remini has performed exceptionally well" versus return expectations and that Brightcove "has recently shown encouraging progress."
  • Co-CFO Enrico Martinelli said, "For Q3, total revenue was $780 million, up 125%," and added, "Q3 operating income totaled $172 million" while "adjusted operating income reached $424 million."

Outlook

  • Co-CFO Martinelli provided Q4 guidance: "For Q4, we expect revenue to be in the range of $984 million to $1 billion" and "We expect adjusted operating income to be in the range of $470 million to $490 million," adding that this "represents an adjusted operating income margin of 48% at the midpoint."
  • Co-CFO Martinelli described the margin setup: "The implied sequential decline in this margin reflects the incorporation of the Airtable and Miro cost bases into our financials," while also stating, "We expect margins, excluding these businesses to expand both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter."
  • Co-CFO Martinelli raised full-year expectations versus prior-quarter guidance: "For the full financial year of 2026, this outlook implies revenue of between $3.07 billion and $3.09 billion" (vs. prior guidance of $2.78 billion to $2.82 billion) and "full year 2026 adjusted operating income of $1.58 billion to $1.6 billion" (vs. $1.46 billion to $1.51 billion).
  • Co-CFO Martinelli clarified deal inclusion: "Specifically, it includes a full quarter contribution from Airtable and Miro's contribution from October '26, but no contribution from the pending Mailchimp acquisition."

Financial Results

  • Co-CFO Martinelli said Airtable was partially consolidated in Q3: "Of this total, $38 million was attributable to Airtable, which was consolidated into our financials from September 4," and also said, "Airtable contributed $10 million to adjusted operating income."
  • Co-CFO Martinelli detailed profitability mechanics: "Operating income as a percentage of revenue was 22%, down from 37% in Q3 '25," while "Adjusted operating income margin was 54%, expanding 1 percentage point compared to Q3 2025," adding the GAAP margin decline was "primarily due to a $149 million increase in amortization of intangible assets" including "a $65 million catch-up charge relating to prior periods."
  • Co-CFO Martinelli highlighted financing costs and EPS: "Interest expense was $107 million," "Diluted earnings per share was $0.13" and "adjusted earnings per share was $0.42."
  • Co-CFO Martinelli described cash flow and leverage: "In Q3, net cash from operating activities totaled $261 million," "At quarter end, the carrying amount of long-term debt was $4.91 billion," "Net debt fell by $187 million during the quarter to $4 billion," and "Leverage ratio stood at 2.1x."

Q&A

  • Eric Sheridan, Goldman Sachs: Asked how Bending Spoons decides to reinvest in slower assets vs. optimize for margin/cash flow; CEO Ferrari said, "our investment...is completely independent of organic revenue growth" and added, "everything we do...is aimed at compounding earnings and free cash flows per share as rapidly as possible with a multi-decade view."
  • Eric Sheridan, Goldman Sachs: Asked about debt vs. equity for M&A; CEO Ferrari said the company prioritizes debt while staying prudent, citing "keeping leverage ratio in the 2 to 3 range," and added equity is used when it helps "keep leverage ratio lower" or "go after a larger target."
  • Kirk Materne, Evercore ISI: Asked how the playbook changes for enterprise/sales-led acquisitions (Airtable, Miro, Mailchimp); CEO Ferrari said Mailchimp is "primarily...SMEs, and it's almost fully self-serve," and added the biggest differences are "whether a business is primarily self-serve versus sales-led."
  • Alec Brondolo, Wells Fargo: Asked about AOL churn from pricing changes and drivers of 5% Q4 organic growth; CEO Ferrari said AOL changes had "modest one-off churn" and that Q4 organic improvement is expected from "AOL, Eventbrite and Vimeo," while "Airtable and Miro...will contribute approximately 1 percentage point to guidance."
  • Omar Dessouky, BofA: Asked whether AI agents could increase consumer subscription cancellations; CEO Ferrari said, "only about 1/3 of our revenues from consumer subscriptions" and added, "we could not find even the slightest impact" across retention indicators, while cautioning, "it's reasonable to expect that at some point...we may see a little bit of deterioration."
  • Bryan Smilek, JPMorgan: Asked about Eventbrite advertising and subscription roadmap; CEO Ferrari said post-checkout ads drove "a nice uplift in advertising revenue" with "absolutely no impact on engagement or retention," and described tested subscriptions for attendees (fee waivers) and organizers (marketing features).
  • Stefan Slowinski, BNP Paribas: Asked why Mailchimp can deliver required returns and whether M&A pace slows; CEO Ferrari said, "We see substantial opportunity to improve both revenue and cost," expects the deal to complete "sometime in the first part of 2027," and added operational capacity remains a constraint but "we feel reasonably good about it."
  • Mark Shmulik, Bernstein: Asked about learnings from AOL ad stack migration; CEO Ferrari said disruption reduced organic growth by "maybe 1 percentage points higher or 1 or 2" absent disruption, and added, "We're now back to the pre-transition impression pricing."
  • Lloyd Walmsley, Mizuho: Asked if annual M&A deployment could exceed $4B-$5B and about Berkshire; CEO Ferrari said, "we have a wonderful trusting partnership" with Berkshire, and on deployment added, "we could deploy more than $4 billion, $5 billion next year," while also saying, "I would still encourage investors to be cautious" and that "$5 billion on average yearly is a reasonable assumption."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, pressing on sustainability and new risks (e.g., AI-driven cancellations, integration pace, and Mailchimp pricing), including Dessouky calling AI agents "a reasonable concern for an investor to have" as echoed by CEO Ferrari.
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and confident in Q&A, using phrases such as CEO Ferrari’s "we feel very confident" on no AI cancellation signal and "we feel pretty good" on operational capacity, while acknowledging constraints like "operational capacity is a potential bottleneck."
  • Versus Q2, management messaging shifted from first-call model explanation to execution updates and larger-scale M&A, with more direct discussion of integration complexity and capital-market tools (bond issuance, PIPE).

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 reported "revenue increased 125% to $780 million" versus Q2 "revenue increased 126% to $704 million," while organic growth stayed at "3%" in both quarters.
  • Full-year 2026 guidance was increased in Q3 to "$3.07 billion to $3.09 billion" revenue and "$1.58 billion to $1.6 billion" adjusted operating income, compared with Q2 guidance of "$2.78 billion to $2.82 billion" revenue and "$1.46 billion to $1.51 billion" adjusted operating income.
  • Q2 discussed Airtable as pending; Q3 confirmed, "These acquisitions have now closed" (Airtable and Miro) and introduced the pending Mailchimp agreement.
  • Analysts’ focus broadened from Q2’s Airtable close timing and hardware exposure (Tractive) toward Q3 questions on enterprise go-to-market, subscription defensibility amid AI agents, and capital structure strategy.

Risks and Concerns

  • Co-CFO Martinelli said Remini faces pressure from "historically relatively low retention rates," "dependence on viral spikes for user acquisition" and "increased competition in the AI image generation market," adding it may continue to reduce organic growth as it declines in portfolio size.
  • CEO Ferrari described short-term disruption risk from ad-tech transitions at AOL, stating the company expected disruption and saw it, while saying it was "short-lived" and that impression pricing was restored.
  • CEO Ferrari acknowledged potential longer-term subscription risk from AI agents, saying, "I would be responsible if I said it's impossible this ever impacts Bending Spoons," while also stating, "so far, absolutely no signal whatsoever."

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized that Q3 combined triple-digit reported growth with a steady 3% organic growth rate, while expanding the acquisition pipeline from closed deals (Airtable and Miro) to a new pending transaction (Mailchimp). Co-CFO guidance lifted full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted operating income ranges versus Q2, while flagging that Q4 margins incorporate Airtable and Miro cost bases and exclude Mailchimp. In Q&A, CEO Ferrari repeatedly framed capital allocation, financing mix, and reinvestment decisions around compounding per-share earnings and free cash flow, while addressing investor concerns on integration capacity, ad-tech disruption, and potential AI-driven subscription cancellations.

Read the full Earnings Call Transcript

data.title: Boeing may be considering additional layoffs, union says after meeting
data.description:
Boeing (BA) management has left open the possibility that additional rounds of layoffs could be coming, according to the company's engineering and technicians union, following a routine meeting with the company's senior engineering managers to discuss workforce issues, The Seattle Times reported late Thursday.

Boeing (BA) announced plans earlier this month to ​cut 5% of its commercial airplanes division's ~50K employees through attrition ​and layoffs, saying it needed to moderate its planned production increases for its 737 MAX jet to allow its factories and suppliers time to stabilize operations and that it would notify impacted workers in December.

The Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace union said the meeting left unanswered questions about how many union members were likely to be affected, which rolescould be cut, and "whether this will be the only round of layoffs."

"The Boeing engineering managers said they had not yet determined those facts, which our committee found both surprising and frustrating," SPEEA said.

The company's engineering managers told the union at the meeting that affected workers would be notified on December 9 but said "Boeing didn't know" when asked if this was the only date for layoff notices, a union spokesperson reportedly told Reuters.

Boeing (BA) managers told ​union officials that "employment ​at all Boeing ⁠Commercial Airplanes sites is under review, but layoffs won't necessarily impact all sites," SEEPA said it told its ~17K members.

SPEEA also said it has an annual attrition rate of 4.9%, meaning "attrition alone will not meet the short-term need to reduce the workforce."

data.title: S&P 500 is near a bottom, but breadth still shows final low is not there yet – BTIG’s Krinsky
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is nearing a tactical bottom around the 7,000 level, though market breadth suggests the final low has not yet been reached, according to Jonathan Krinsky, chief market technician at BTIG.

With the index pushing down 7,100, the top end of BTIG's targeted range, Krinsky invoked an old Japanese proverb, saying, "Tactically the downside is 80% full here."

He expects a short-term bottom should materialize in the next few days around the 7,000 level.

Short-term capitulation indicators are flashing, according to the strategist. The Daily Sentiment Index for the S&P 500 (SP500) closed at 10, the lowest level since the Liberation Day lows in April 2025, while the VIX (VIX) curve inverted by over 6 points, also the most since spring 2025.

Krinsky believes that from the S&P 500’s (SP500) 7,000 level, the market "could see a 4-5% recovery, which would take it back up towards the 200-day moving average” at 7,348.

However, this is not the final low, Krinsky warned, pointing to market breadth as the key reason.

Currently, 50% of S&P 500 (SP500) stocks remain above their 50-day moving averages, he noted.

"In the last 30 years, if we look at all S&P 500 pullbacks of 8% or more, the median reading of names above their 50-day MA is 11%," the strategist explained, adding that "it would be unprecedented to be putting in a final low here with half of the S&P 500 still above the 50-day MA.”

Apple's (AAPL) resilience near all-time highs also signals more downside ahead, according to Krinsky.

Looking at all S&P 500 (SP500) bottoms since 2015, the closest Apple (AAPL) was to a 52-week high was -11.8% in August 2024, with the median at -23% below 52-week highs.

"It would be unprecedented to make a final low with the world's biggest stock so close to an all-time high," he said.

The strategist continues to see downside risk ahead for Apple (AAPL), calling it "likely part of a bigger washout."

S&P 500 ETFs: (SPY), (VOO), (IVV), (RSP), (SSO), (UPRO), (SH), (SDS), (SPXU), (FXAIX), (VFIAX), (VFFSX), and (SWPPX).

data.title: HIVE Digital and BitGo among financial stocks to join Russell Microcap; Strive and Sachem Capital to exit
data.description:
As part of its 2026 semi-annual reconstitution, FTSE Russell released preliminary additions and deletions for the Russell Microcap Indexes, with several notable financial stocks set to enter or exit after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11.

Financial sector stocks scheduled to be added to the Russell Microcap Index include HIVE Digital Technologies (NASDAQ:HIVE), BitGo Holdings (NYSE:BTGO), Robostrategy (NASDAQ:BOT), Private Bancorp of America (NASDAQ:PBAM), and West Coast Community Bancorp (NASDAQ:WCCB).

Financial stocks set to be removed from the Russell Microcap Index include Strive (NASDAQ:ASST), Sachem Capital (NYSE:SACH), Granite Point Mortgage Trust (NYSE:GPMT), Porch Group (NASDAQ:PRCH), and eHealth (NASDAQ:EHTH).

The newly reconstituted indexes will take effect after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11, 2026, following preliminary list updates scheduled for Nov. 20, Nov. 27, and Dec. 4.
